protocol: generation-based (greedy 24 tok, gold value/alias substring match, per-group AND/OR test_condition); condition_queries precondition filter omitted. base/in_context/cake score the SAME first-100 shuffled(seed=0) examples (no skip logic). ROME uses a different sample: eval_rome_ripple.py skips any example whose edit prompt lacks ' is ' or whose subject can't be extracted by a crude 'text after last " of "' heuristic, so ROME's 100 edits are NOT guaranteed identical to the other three, and the heuristic may extract wrong subject spans for kept edits.
key_findings: RAG (in-context) wins the aggregate — the model reasons over the new fact in context, so ripples propagate.

ROME scores ~base (0.078 vs 0.073) on this run, but ROME's sample and subject spans come from a crude heuristic that both filters edits and may mis-extract subjects, so its number is indicative only, not a rigorously matched comparison (see sampling_caveat).
CAKE is mid on propagation (0.307) and WINS Subject_Aliasing (0.816 — an alias of the edited subject still hits the slot).
CAKE is WORST of all four on preservation (0.049): it over-fires, destroying unrelated same-subject facts (Relation_Specificity 0.061, Forgetfulness 0.036) — worse than the unedited base.
This is the measured, published-benchmark confirmation of CAKE's structural weakness: retrieval-not-rederivation cannot chain edits and over-writes neighbors.
sampling_caveat: FAIRNESS LIMITATION: base/RAG/CAKE share an identical query set; ROME's set may differ due to subject-extraction filtering. ROME's low score (0.078, ~base) is therefore a weaker claim than the other three — treat ROME here as indicative, not a rigorously matched comparison. The RAG-vs-CAKE contrast (identical queries) is sound.
